nodes.label: ExpressBackend
nodes.rationale: Runs actor-ts routes through Express. Chosen for an existing middleware investment, team familiarity, or an incremental migration - not for perceived simplicity, since both backends are equally simple from the actor-ts side.

nodes.label: ExpressBackendOptions
nodes.rationale: withMaxBodyBytes raises the shared 1 MiB body cap; withApp hands the backend a bring-your-own Express app, which is also where X-Forwarded-* handling and TLS (Node https) are configured.

nodes.label: Express middleware ecosystem
nodes.rationale: Express middleware wraps the actor-ts routes, so requests flow through it first. This is the main reason to pick Express over Fastify; without that need Fastify is faster (40-60K vs 150-200K req/sec).

nodes.label: WebSocket handshake through the Express app
nodes.rationale: A websocket() route registers as an ordinary Express GET and the upgrade is dispatched through the app, so app.use runs for the handshake. A middleware that answers cancels the handshake; one that calls next() reaches the framework's own upgrade guard, which still has the last word. A rejection's body only reaches the client on runtimes that allow writing to a hijacked upgrade socket - Bun and Node do, Deno does not.
